saints.name: The Presentation of the Lord
saints.title: Feast of the Lord
saints.shortBlurb: Forty days after Christmas the Church keeps the day the Infant Christ was brought to the Temple and hailed by Simeon as a light to the nations…
biography: Forty days after his birth, in obedience to the law of Moses, Mary and Joseph brought the Child Jesus to the Temple in Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, offering the sacrifice of the poor, a pair of turtledoves. There the aged Simeon took him in his arms and praised him as 'a light to the revelation of the Gentiles', and the prophetess Anna gave thanks to God.

The feast is among the Church's oldest: the pilgrim Egeria saw it kept with a procession at Jerusalem in the fourth century, and in 542 the Emperor Justinian extended it through the East in thanksgiving for the end of a great pestilence. The Greeks named it Hypapante, the 'Meeting' of the Lord with Simeon and Anna.

In the West it appears in seventh-century Rome under the name Purification of the Blessed Virgin; Pope Sergius I gave it a procession, and from the blessing and carrying of candles, common since the eleventh century, comes the English name Candlemas. Since 1969 it is kept as the Presentation of the Lord, and in 1997 John Paul II made it the World Day for Consecrated Life.
saints.knownFor: The presentation of the Infant Christ in the Temple and the canticle of Simeon.
